• All longitudes are equal in length.

rows: All longitudes are equal in length
Tropics mark overhead Sun limits; Circles mark polar day/night
82.5°E serves as the basis for IST

items: Indian Standard Time (IST) meridian (82.5°E) is a very frequent question in geography sections.
Remember the key figure: Distance between latitudes is approximately 111 km.
Do not confuse latitude and longitude lengths: latitudes vary (Equator is longest), whereas all longitudes are equal.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Equator is the longest latitude line on Earth.
The approximate distance between consecutive latitudes is 111 km.
Unlike latitudes, all lines of longitude are equal in length.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is determined based on the 82.5°E longitude meridian.
The Tropics define the geographic limits of the overhead Sun.
Polar day and night phenomena occur beyond the Arctic and Antarctic circles.
